obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106: group
basis: The holding company is a publicly traded registrant that files Form 10-K; Item 106 has no size exemption

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05: group
basis: SEC registrant; the disclosure committee decides materiality of cybersecurity incidents in every division

obligation: SOX section 404, including 404(b): group
basis: A large accelerated filer (17 CFR 240.12b-2), so the 7262(c) exemption does not apply and the auditor attests. The ERP, HCM and treasury are in scope for IT general controls

obligation: Federal Reserve computer-security incident notification: group
basis: No subsidiary is a bank or savings association, so the group is not a bank holding company or savings and loan holding company (12 CFR 225.2(b), (c)(1))

obligation: Interagency Guidelines, 12 CFR Part 225 Appendix F: group
basis: Same reason as N55-R04. GLBA safeguards for the insurers come from the state insurance authority (15 U.S.C. 6805(a)(6)); see N52-R01

obligation: HIPAA: the group health plan (covered entity) and the holding company as plan sponsor
basis: The self-insured medical plan has about 38,000 participants and a third-party administrator, so it is a group health plan and a covered entity. The sponsor's plan administration unit receives PHI beyond summary and enrollment information (appeals, stop-loss claims), so the plan-document rules apply in full: 164.504(f)(2) and 164.314(b)

obligation: CIRCIA: group
basis: Proposed rule only; reporting is not mandatory. Tracked for the insurance and health care sector criteria

obligation: Florida insurance holding company system: annual enterprise risk report and examination of affiliates
basis: The holding company is the ultimate controlling person of two Florida-domiciled insurers; each insurer registers by April 1 and the holding company files the enterprise risk report with Florida as lead state; the Office may examine affiliates, including the SCSP

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act and other state breach laws: all entities
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171; each state where affected individuals reside
basis: The group holds personal information of employees, former employees, claimants, policyholders and patients in Florida and other states; Florida is the worked example, including the third-party agent duty in 501.171(6)

obligation: SEC public-company cybersecurity disclosure (same duty as N55-R01 and N55-R02): group
basis: Recorded under N55-R01 and N55-R02; the divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: all entities
basis: The insurers are persons providing insurance, assigned to the state insurance authority (15 U.S.C. 6805(a)(6)); the entity register shows no nonbank lender or other financial institution under FTC jurisdiction

obligation: State insurance data security laws based on NAIC Model #668: the insurers
citation: NAIC Model #668 as enacted (Alabama, South Carolina; Tennessee in part)
applies: Yes (Alabama, South Carolina, Tennessee in part)
basis: Both insurers are licensees in all 6 states; the model's duties bind them where a licensed state has enacted it. Florida, Georgia and North Carolina have general breach statutes only. Text varies by state; insurance counsel confirms each enacted version

obligation: Model #668 sec. 3P and 4F: the holding company as the insurers' Third-Party Service Provider
basis: The holding company processes claims payments and runs identity for the insurers under the 2017 intercompany agreement, so it maintains, processes and accesses their nonpublic information as a person that is not itself a licensee

obligation: Model #668 sec. 4I annual certification: the insurers
basis: The certification applies to insurers domiciled in an enacting state; both insurers are domiciled in Florida, which has not enacted the model

obligation: Model #668 sec. 6E reinsurer notices: the insurers
basis: The insurers cede risk to reinsurers and assume none

obligation: Model #668 sec. 9A(2) HIPAA deemer: the insurers
basis: The insurers write personal auto, homeowners and workers' compensation coverage, which are excepted benefits (42 U.S.C. 300gg-91(c)(1)) outside the HIPAA definition of health plan (45 CFR 160.103), so the insurers are not HIPAA-regulated and the deemer cannot apply

obligation: GLBA safeguards and privacy: the insurers
applies: Yes (through Florida as State of domicile)
basis: The insurers are financial institutions holding consumers' nonpublic personal information; safeguards for persons providing insurance are enforced by the State insurance authority of the State of domicile, here Florida. Any Florida Office of Insurance Regulation safeguards rule is confirmed by counsel

obligation: NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of AI Systems by Insurers: the insurers
applies: Yes (North Carolina); applied to all Insurance AI by group choice
basis: Among the 6 licensed states, only North Carolina has adopted the bulletin (NAIC map, 2026-04-01). The insurers use AI in claims triage and fraud scoring, photo estimating and bill review

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation: all entities
basis: No group entity holds a New York insurance or banking license

obligation: Bank information security guidelines and other bank and credit union rules (N52-R02, N52-R09, N52-R10): all entities
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B and D; 12 CFR 225 App. F; 12 CFR Part 748
basis: The entity register lists no bank, savings association or credit union

obligation: SEC Regulation S-P and Regulation S-ID (N52-R05, N52-R06): all entities
basis: The entity register lists no broker-dealer, investment company, investment adviser or transfer agent

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Health Care Services
basis: A health care provider that transmits claims, eligibility and remittance as standard electronic transactions through its clearinghouse is a covered entity (45 CFR 160.103). No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: the holding company as business associate of Health Care Services
basis: Under the 2021 BAA the holding company creates, receives, maintains and transmits Health Care Services ePHI: identity for the clinic EHR through SYS-G1, patient refund files through SYS-G6, and shared infrastructure

obligation: HIPAA: the insurers
basis: Workers' compensation, liability (including automobile liability) and automobile medical payment insurance are excepted benefits, which the HIPAA definition of health plan excludes. Claimant medical information is still nonpublic information under Model #668 sec. 3K(3)

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Health Care Services
basis: Covered entity. Work-injury disclosures to workers' compensation insurers, including the group's insurer, rely on 164.512(l); work-related findings to employers rely on 164.512(b)(1)(v); minimum necessary and routine-disclosure protocols apply (164.502(b), 164.514(d)(3))

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: the holding company as business associate
basis: Uses and disclosures of Health Care Services PHI are limited to what the BAA permits

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Health Care Services
basis: Own notices to individuals, HHS and media as a covered entity

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: the holding company as business associate
basis: Notice to Health Care Services as its business associate; the 2021 BAA sets 10 days

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: the group health plan
basis: The plan is a covered entity separate from Health Care Services and makes its own notices

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025): Health Care Services, the plan and the holding company
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD records): all entities
basis: The Health Care Services service line list has no federally assisted substance use disorder program; no other division provides care

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule: all entities
basis: 16 CFR 318.1 excludes HIPAA covered entities and business associates acting as such; Health Care Services and the plan are covered entities and the holding company acts as a business associate

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Health Care Services
basis: Health Care Services accepts Medicare and Medicaid (federal financial assistance) and uses the EHR vendor's triage and sepsis alert, whose inputs include age and sex

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness conditions: Health Care Services
basis: The clinics are urgent care and occupational medicine physician offices, which are not among the certified provider types the rules cover

obligation: HIPAA applicability to social assistance: all entities
basis: No group entity is a social assistance organization

obligation: Federal employment discrimination law applied to AI in hiring: group
basis: The group employs 45,000 people and its HCM recruiting module had a vendor resume screening feature switched on in 2026-03

obligation: Florida recording consent (worked example of state law): Health Care Services and group
basis: Interception is lawful when all parties consent; relevant to the proposed AI scribe and to meeting transcription by the AI assistant

obligation: Colorado AI law (SB26-189): group
basis: Not in effect during this assessment; rechecked in P10 before any AI use in employment, insurance or health care decisions

obligation: Intercompany services agreements: holding company with the insurers and with Health Care Services
basis: The agreements set the shared services the subsidiaries rely on; the 2017 agreement carries no security, service level or incident notice terms

obligation: Business associate agreement: holding company with Health Care Services
basis: Breach notice within 10 days and the required BAA terms

obligation: SOC 2 assurance requested by customers and affiliates: occupational health employer portal and SCSP
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; client contracts
basis: Employer clients of the occupational health portal ask for a SOC 2 report; the insurers' sec. 4F oversight of the holding company needs an assurance source
